summary: A compiler for linear-optical quantum computing places small subcircuits on the best region of an imperfect interferometer mesh and routes photons to good input/output ports, instead of spreading the computation over the entire chip. Optimizing directly for coincidence rate under beam-splitter, loss and phase-noise imperfections improves coincidence rates by up to 33.2% over existing compilers.
motivation: Spatially varying loss and phase noise in photonic meshes strongly degrade accuracy, and current compilers ignore where on the chip a subcircuit is placed.
method: An efficient subcircuit-compilation method that trades routing losses from imperfect beam-splitter reflectivities against port transmission losses to maximize the coincidence rate.
result: Coincidence rates rise by up to 33.2% across benchmarks, with better robustness to phase noise than existing methods.
